en.name: Cashew butter
en.summary: Cashew butter keeps about 3 months in the pantry and does not need to be refrigerated. That is a good deal shorter than almond butter, and the reason is the nut: cashews are soft, high in oil and mild in flavour, so rancidity shows up sooner and hides less well.
en.pantry: A cool, dark cupboard gives about 3 months, and refrigeration is not required. Cashew butter separates and hardens less dramatically than almond butter because cashews grind so smoothly, but the oil still rises — stir it back in rather than pouring it off. Keep the jar away from the hob and out of direct light, which are what turn nut oils, and buy the size you will finish in a season rather than the big tub, because three months goes quickly on a jar you use for one recipe.
en.fridge: No refrigerator timeline is published for cashew butter, and the product does not need refrigerating — the pantry figure assumes a cupboard. In a hot kitchen, or if a jar is going to sit for weeks between uses, the fridge is a reasonable way to slow the oil turning; the cost is that it sets firm and needs to come back to room temperature before it spreads. Whichever you choose, use a clean dry knife every time, because moisture at the surface is what starts mould.
en.freezer: No freezer figure is given for cashew butter. Freezing does no harm and it will be safe indefinitely at −18 °C (0 °F), but no timeline is published, so this page will not invent one. For a large batch of home-ground cashew butter, freezing portions in small jars is defensible; for a shop jar the three-month window and a smaller purchase are the simpler answer.
en.thawing: Thaw a frozen jar in the fridge or at cool room temperature, then stir it thoroughly before use.
spoilage: A sharp, bitter or paint-like smell — rancid nut oil.
A bitter aftertaste that was not there when the jar was opened.
Mould at the surface or around the rim, usually from a wet knife.
A fermented or alcoholic smell, which means moisture has got in.
tips: Stir separated oil back in; do not pour it off.
Use a clean dry knife every time.
Buy small jars — three months is shorter than most nut butters.
Keep it away from the hob; heat is what turns nut oil fastest.

faq.q: How long does cashew butter keep?
faq.a: About 3 months in a cool, dark cupboard. It does not need to be refrigerated.
No. The pantry figure assumes a cupboard. Refrigeration slows the oil turning but makes it hard to spread.

faq.q: Why does cashew butter keep less time than almond butter?
faq.a: Cashews are softer and milder, so their oil turns sooner and there is less flavour to mask it when it does.

zh.name: 腰果醬
zh.summary: 腰果醬放常溫櫥櫃約可放 3 個月，而且不需要冷藏。這比杏仁醬短不少，原因在堅果本身：腰果質地軟、含油高、味道溫和，所以油耗來得更早，也更藏不住。
zh.pantry: 陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 3 個月，不需要冷藏。腰果磨得非常細滑，所以它分層和變硬的程度不像杏仁醬那麼誇張，但油還是會浮上來——請拌回去，不要倒掉。罐子遠離爐台、避免直射光，那兩樣正是讓堅果油變質的原因；而且請買一季內用得完的尺寸，不要買大桶，因為對一罐只為某道食譜而買的醬來說，三個月過得很快。
zh.fridge: 腰果醬沒有公布的冷藏期限，產品本身也不需要冷藏——櫥櫃那個數字本來就是以不冷藏為前提。如果廚房很熱，或一罐要放好幾週才用一次，冷藏是延緩油脂變質的合理做法；代價是它會變硬，要回到室溫才抹得開。不論放哪裡，每次都用乾淨乾燥的刀，因為表面的水分正是發霉的起點。
zh.freezer: 這裡沒有給腰果醬的冷凍數字。冷凍不會傷害它，在 −18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，但沒有公布的期限，所以本頁不會憑空生一個。自己大量現磨的話，分裝小罐冷凍說得過去；市售一罐的話，三個月的期限加上買小一點，是更簡單的答案。
zh.thawing: 冷凍過的罐子放冷藏或涼爽室溫解凍，使用前充分攪拌。
spoilage: 聞起來刺鼻、發苦或有油漆味——堅果油走油耗。
出現剛開罐時沒有的苦後味。
表面或罐口長霉，通常來自沾濕的刀。
有發酵味或酒精味，代表水分跑進去了。
tips: 分離的油要拌回去，不要倒掉。
每次都用乾淨乾燥的刀。
買小罐——三個月比多數堅果醬都短。
遠離爐台；高溫讓堅果油變質最快。

faq.a: 陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 3 個月，不需要冷藏。
不需要。櫥櫃那個數字本來就是以不冷藏為前提。冷藏能延緩油脂變質，但會變得很難抹。

faq.q: 腰果醬為什麼比杏仁醬短？
faq.a: 腰果比較軟、味道也比較清淡，油脂變質得更早，而且變質時沒有足夠的風味可以掩蓋。
